metadata.title: ICILS 2023: Digital kompetanse og algoritmisk tenkning hos norske niendeklassinger

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report is based on ICILS 2023, which uses a complex, multi-stage sampling design with stratification and clustering at the school/classroom levels. For Norway, the report states that student participation is “vektet data” with 87% student participation, indicating that analyses use survey weights to produce representative estimates for the national target population. The report also describes that schools were randomly selected by IEA’s Data Processing and Research Center (DPC) and that classes were drawn within schools, with reserves used to meet participation requirements. The manuscript does not name a specific weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT), and it does not report replicate-weight methods; therefore, replicate-weight usage cannot be confirmed from the text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a national descriptive/comparative report presenting ICILS achievement scale results (means, standard deviations, and proficiency-level distributions) and questionnaire percentages, rather than training predictive ML models on PV-based cognitive outcomes. Plausible Values handling is therefore not applicable in the sense required for empirical ML/predictive pipelines on PVs. Missing-data handling is not described at the level of an imputation/deletion protocol for the analytic dataset, which is a reporting gap for methodological transparency, though the report focuses on published ICILS scoring and reporting conventions.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the ICILS 2023 national sample of Norwegian 9th-grade students participating in the ICILS 2023 digital competence (DK) and algorithmic thinking (AT) assessments, with exclusions for students with physical/psychological disabilities and students with short residence who did not master Norwegian. The report also applies ICILS participation requirements at school and student levels (minimum 85% participation thresholds), and it reports weighted participation rates (“vektet data”) for students and teachers. No further student-level analytic filtering rules (e.g., complete-case rules for specific questionnaire items) are specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This ICILS 2023 Norway national report summarizes students’ performance in two ICILS 2023 assessments for 9th graders: Digital Competence (DK) and Algorithmic Thinking (AT), alongside student and teacher questionnaire results. DK is reported on a scale anchored to the 2013 international mean (500, SD=100) and in 2023 has an international mean of 476 (SD=88); Norway’s DK mean is 502, significantly above the international average, with 60% of Norwegian students at DK proficiency level 2 or higher. AT is reported on a separate scale with an international mean of 483; Norway’s AT mean is 485, around the international average, with 66% at AT level 2 or higher. The report also documents digital divides by gender and socioeconomic background: girls outperform boys in DK (and the gender gap is larger in Norway than in other Nordic countries), and socioeconomic background is positively associated with both DK and AT. Methodologically, the report is descriptive/comparative and does not present an ML predictive modeling pipeline; it therefore does not report PV-handling or ML performance metrics.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse with respect to ML methodology because the document is a national descriptive/comparative report of ICILS 2023 results rather than an empirical machine-learning study. It reports achievement scale summaries (means, standard deviations, proficiency-level distributions) and questionnaire percentages, but it does not specify an ML target variable, model training procedure, or predictive evaluation metrics. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and PV-based predictive modeling are intentionally left empty, while survey-weight usage is inferred from the stated “vektet data” participation rates and the complex sampling description.
